title: Draft schema for x-bte annotation refactor
description: Manually-written schema for x-bte annotation refactor. Work-in-progress.

info.description: Required, fixed property in OpenAPI schema. Provides metadata about the API.

x-bte.description: Optional property to provide API info that the tool needs for querying or post-processing.

batch_size_limit.description: Maximum number of input IDs per request (if an annotation's request_info.support_batch: true.

request_rate_limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per minute from each client.

primary_key_edge_attributes.description: List of TRAPI edge-attribute keys (attribute_type_id) that distinguish unique edges. If attribute X is listed here and two constructed TRAPI edges only differ by attribute X's value, the tool should be keep both of them as separate edges.

x-bte-annotations.description: One or more x-bte annotations go here. One x-bte annotation describes a subset of data available using the API (semantics), how to query for this data, and how to process the response (assumed to be JSON). The main properties that define a unique x-bte annotation are core 'metaedge' info: input category, predicate, qualifier-set, and output category. Keys are user-defined names; usually, they note the dataset and type of biological relationship.

^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$.description: This is the subschema for a single annotation. Properties are snake_case.

response_field_root.description: Response-fields are specified using the dot-notation path or other valid JSONata query. If every response-field/JSONata query in this annotation involves the same root path, that root can be specified using this optional property. If this property is used, then all other dot-notation paths in this annotation SHOULD start from the specified root. For JSONata queries, the tool will assume that the specified root points to an iterable, so all JSONata queries in this annotation SHOULD be scoped to the individual items of that iterable. Format: don't include a trailing dot.

inputs.description: Describes the input biological entities (and their IDs). These are put in the API request to retrieve data on their relationships with other biological entities.

use_all_namespaces.description: Only use when the 'namespaces' array has >1 item. If an input biological entity has synonymous IDs from >1 ID namespace listed in the 'namespaces' section, should the tool generate queries using all of those IDs (true)? True implies that the API may have different data for the same biological entity under different IDs from different namespaces, and you want to retrieve all of that data. Or should the tool only use the IDs for 1 namespace - the first in the 'namespaces' section that it has IDs for (false)? False implies that the API has already done an 'entity-resolution' step and an ID from any namespace would retrieve the same data. If this property isn't specified, the tool defaults to 'false' behavior.
use_all_namespaces.$comment: While `outputs` also has this property, the description is different.

namespaces.description: List of possible ID namespaces for input biological entities. They should be in order of preference (see 'use_all_namespaces' property's description).
namespaces.$comment: outputs also has this property. Right now, I'm defining the two separately because the required properties are different.

request_prefix.description: Sometimes, in requests, the API expects prefixed IDs with DIFFERENT prefixes than what's specified in the 'prefix' property or with a delimiter between prefix and ID that isn't a colon. In these situations, the annotator should specify here the prefix AND delimiter that the API expects.

match_field.description: If the annotation's request_info.support_batch is true, there should be a response-field that specifies the matched input ID. In this scenario, this property SHOULD be used to specify the dot-notation path to this response-field or other valid JSONata query. The returned value (of this response-field or JSONata query) SHOULD be an ID in namespace-standard format OR a CURIE (ID-namespace-standard-prefix:ID-in-namespace-standard-format), so it can be matched with the input biological entities' IDs. However, it is expected and fine that JSONata queries sometimes return empty strings (ex: capture regex for a specific namespace's IDs may not return anything because the match_field's value is actually from a different namespace).

if.$comment: If use_all_namespaces is present, the namespaces array should have >=2 items.

predicate.description: This is the (semantic) type of the relationship between the input and output biological entities. The value must be a predicate in the biolink-model: it should be the most specific predicate that matches the relationship. Predicates labeled 'mixin' should be used carefully (read yaml spec before using). The format is snake_case, no prefix. Validation is currently just on format, so it doesn't check whether the value actually exists in the biolink-model version the tool is using.
predicate.$comment: For full validation, this would need enum of biolink-model predicates. And would need to be maintained, up-to-date with biolink-model version the tool is using.

qualifiers.description: This is 1 static set of biolink-model qualifiers that add nuance and detail to the relationship between the input and output biological entities. The keys should be specific qualifiers from the biolink-model, and the values should be from the biolink-model enums for those qualifiers. No prefixes are needed for keys or values.
qualifiers.$comment: Not specifying every recommended qualifier_type_id right now. TBH I'm not sure what a complete set would be. So giving the basic format. qualifier_type_id are snake_case and generally end in '_qualifier'. values are snake-case.

outputs.description: Describes the output biological entities (and their IDs). These should be in the API's response along with any data on the relationship between the input and output biological entities.

namespaces.description: List of possible ID namespaces for output biological entities. Multiple namespaces should be listed in order of preference. When the tool is parsing one record (the response data for the relationship between one input and one output biological entity), it'll iterate through the namespace items in order until it successfully retrieves an output ID. The assumption is: if a record has multiple output IDs from multiple namespaces, those IDs all represent the same biological entity so the tool only needs one of those IDs to recognize the output entity.

id_field.description: Specifies the response-field for the output entity's ID. Format: Dot-notation path to this response-field or other valid JSONata query. The returned value (of this response-field or JSONata query) SHOULD be an ID in namespace-standard format OR a CURIE (ID-namespace-standard-prefix:ID-in-namespace-standard-format). However, it is expected and fine that JSONata queries sometimes return empty strings (ex: capture regex for a specific namespace's IDs may not return anything because the id_field's value is actually from a different namespace). Guidelines: (1) If a response-field returns output IDs from multiple namespaces, the returned value (JSONata can be used) MUST be a CURIE. (2) If the response-field only returns output IDs from 1 namespace, the returned value can be an ID (no prefix).

exclude_namespace_combos.description: Only use this property if inputs.namespaces AND outputs.namespaces arrays both have >1 item. If a few input/output ID-namespace combos don't exist in the API's data, these combos can be listed here so the tool can skip them. If this property AND include_namespace_combos are not specified, the tool will assume that the API data may include all possible combos of input and output ID namespaces.

include_namespace_combos.description: Similar to 'exclude_namespace_combos', except this property is for listing combos that exist in the API's data. Annotation writers SHOULD NOT specify both properties in the same annotation (just specify one). There may be edge-cases where it's preferable to use this property over exclude_namespace_combos. Ex: input/output have a LOT of possible ID namespaces but only a small amount of combos actually exist.
include_namespace_combos.$comment: if exclude_namespace_combos is used, then this one shouldn't be used and vice versa. Add logic to schema later?

request_info.description: Info needed to generate the API request. If the request should include a request_body or parameters, this info MUST be specified - either directly under request_info (top-level) OR in by_input_namespace / by_output_namespace. If request_body/parameters exists in the top-level AND in an object within by_input_namespace / by_output_namespace, the version in the 'by' property will be used (overrides top-level, general version).
request_info.$comment: Needs complex validation logic for {request_body, parameters, by_input_namespace, by output_namespace}: at least 1 of these needs to exist. If one of the by_... exist, than no other fields can (VS request_body, parameters can be together). Within by_..., they need at least 1 of {request_body, parameters}.

path.description: Which endpoint the request should be sent to. This MUST be a relative path (from the API server url) listed in the 'paths' section of the OpenAPI/SmartAPI spec.

method.description: Which http method (ex: get vs post) the request should use. This MUST be a method specified for the 'path' endpoint in the 'paths' section of the OpenAPI/SmartAPI spec.

support_batch.description: Can multiple input IDs be sent in 1 request (true) or not (false)

content_type.description: Use this property to specify the content type (aka media type) of the request body. If not specified, the default is 'application/json'. The annotation writer is responsible for specifying a request body that matches this content type.

use_pagination.description: Is this request using API pagination (true), or not (false)? Default is false.
use_pagination.$comment: For now, note info needed for/related to pagination in notes doc. Deciding where this info goes and its format later.

provenance.description: Info on where the biological relationship data comes from (sources) and how it was generated. There are different formats to cover a range of scenarios.
provenance.$comment: complex!!! one of 3 schemas (two object, 1 array). Have some nested parts that are kinda repetitive, can make $ref to $def. BE CAREFUL OF RECURSIVE SCHEMAS, $REF TO ANOTHER $REF.

oneOf.description: In this case, the annotator wants to assign different provenance info depending on input/output ID namespace. The annotator can use this format to map different input/output ID-namespace combos to different structured provenance data. All possible input/output ID-namespace combos should be included in this mapping.

items.$comment: subschema basic_provenance_info also uses 'unevaluatedProperties: false'. Hopefully it's okay to have twice. If it's not, read https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/object#extending

oneOf.description: In this case, there is an API response-field with string values (basically keywords), which provides specific provenance info for each record. One record is the response data for the relationship between one input and one output biological entity. The annotator can use this format to map the response-field's values to different structured provenance data. All possible values for this response-field should be included in this mapping.

source_field.description: Specifies the response-field that provides specific provenance info. Format: Dot-notation path to this response-field or other valid JSONata query.

mapping.description: Maps response-field's values (must be strings) to structured provenance data

response_mapping.description: Map response-fields to TRAPI edge properties, generally edge attributes. The mapping keys can be (1) keywords (linked to specific ways of parsing the response-field's value and setting up the TRAPI edge property) OR (2) CURIEs (ID-namespace-standard-prefix:ID-in-namespace-standard-format) for the type of data (generally from the biolink-model or a commonly-used ontology). The values should be dot-notation paths to the response-fields or other valid JSONata queries. Advice: users generally want references (publication IDs), publication text snippets (if text-mined), and other structured info.

^([A-Za-z0-9_-.]+):([A-Za-z0-9_-.]+)$.description: mapping keys are CURIEs (ID-namespace-standard-prefix:ID-in-namespace-standard-format) for the type of data (generally from the biolink-model or a commonly-used ontology).

trapi_edge_attributes.description: The response-field's value is a complete set of TRAPI edge-attributes (already in the desired format). The tool should ingest this data without applying changes, EXCEPT in the case of knowledge_level/agent_type. If knowledge_level/agent_type edge-attributes exist in the ingested data, they will be overridden using data from the `provenance` section.

ref_pmid.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more PMIDs of publications that support this biological relationship. These should be put into CURIE format (prefix PMID) and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

ref_url.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more urls to webpages that support this biological relationship. These should be kept as-is and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

ref_pmcid.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more PMCIDs of publications that support this biological relationship. These should be put into CURIE format (prefix PMCID?) and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

ref_clinicaltrials.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more clinical trial NCT IDs that support this biological relationship. These should be put into CURIE format (prefix clinicaltrials, ID should start with NCT) and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

ref_doi.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more DOI for publications that support this biological relationship. These should be put into CURIE format (prefix doi) and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

ref_isbn.description: The response-field's value is 1 or more ISBN for publications that support this biological relationship. These should be put into CURIE format (prefix isbn) and added to the contents of the 'biolink:publications' edge-attribute.

test_examples.description: This section is optional but very useful for testing, so highly recommended to fill out. This is a list of input/output ID pairs that a tool should be able to retrieve from the API using this annotation. These IDs should be in CURIE format (ID-namespace-standard-prefix:ID-in-namespace-standard-format).

if.$comment: If SmartAPI document has the x-bte tag, it SHOULD have the components.x-bte-annotations section.
If SmartAPI document has the components.x-bte-annotations section, it SHOULD have the  x-bte tag.
If SmartAPI document has the info.x-bte section, it SHOULD also have the x-bte tag and components.x-bte-annotations section.

basic_provenance_info.description: This is the simplest case: all data retrieved using this annotation has the same, single set of provenance info.
basic_provenance_info.$comment: add validation logic to this subschema. If api_is_aggregator is present, then sources is not and vice versa! That way source-info is always present. Also don't include any $ref in here.

knowledge_level.description: Biolink-model knowledge level for the data
knowledge_level.$comment: Enum would need to be kept up-to-date with the tool's biolink-model version

agent_type.description: Biolink-model agent type for the data
agent_type.$comment: Enum would need to be kept up-to-date with the tool's biolink-model version

api_is_aggregator.description: If this property is set to true, then the 'sources' property should not be present AND INSTEAD the tool should set the API's infores ID (provided in info.x-translator.infores) as the primary_knowledge_source. If this property is set to false, then the 'sources' property MUST be present to provide annotation-specific TRAPI source info and the tool will add the API infores ID as an aggregator_knowledge_source. If this property isn't specified, the tool defaults to 'false' behavior.

sources.description: List of sources for the data retrieved by this annotation.
sources.$comment: logic needed? If primary, no upstream. If aggregator, need upstream. Don't worry about supporting.

id.description: Should be in infores:ID format, where the resource ID is from Translator's infores registry

role.$comment: Enum would need to be kept up-to-date with the tool's biolink-model version

upstream.description: Use to link a resource to the base resource(s) that it ingested. This property's value(s) should be (infores) ids from other source objects in the 'sources' array.

record_url_field.description: Optional property to specify a response-field that provides urls to the source's webpages. These webpages SHOULD be for specific relationships between input and output biological entities. Format: Dot-notation path to this response-field or other valid JSONata query.

by_fields_subschema.description: Sometimes, parameters/request_body values vary depending on input or output ID namespace - use this property to provide those different values by namespace. Other request_info will be inherited from the top-level request_info properties. The keys are the 'prefix' values for ALL ID namespaces from the corresponding section ('inputs' or 'outputs'). The values are the namespace-specific parameters and/or request_body values. If by_input_namespace is used, then by_output_namespace SHOULD NOT be used, and vice versa. Notes: (1) it'll likely be rare to use by_output_namespace. (2) The annotator may NEED to use by_input_namespace when the API uses non-prefixed IDs and the IDs from different namespaces have the same format (ex: numeric). The annotator could write diff parameters/request_body to match each namespace's IDs to different namespace-specific data fields. This avoids accidentally matching IDs to the wrong namespace's data.

category.description: This is the (semantic) type of biological entities represented by these IDs. The value must be a class (aka node category) in the biolink-model: it should be the most specific class that fits the most biological entities represented in the data. Avoid using classes labeled 'mixin' when possible. The format is PascalCase, no prefix. Validation is currently just on format, so it doesn't check whether the value actually exists in the biolink-model version the tool is using.
category.$comment: For full validation, this would need enum of acceptable biolink-model node categories (not mixins and must be bioentities?). And would need to be maintained, up-to-date with biolink-model version the tool is using.

name_field.description: Optional property to specify a response-field that provides a human-readable name/label for the ID. The tool will use this name for the node if it doesn't find a name/label for the ID using its ID-resolving service. Format: Dot-notation path to this response-field or other valid JSONata query.

parameters.description: Specifies the request parameters. These DO NOT NEED to be specified in endpoint/method's subsection within the 'paths' section of the OpenAPI/SmartAPI spec. The annotation writer has the variables {{input_ids}} (array of IDs w/o prefix) and {{input_curies}} (array of IDs with prefix) to denote where the input IDs go in the parameters (if needed). Jinja2 templating is available to transform those arrays into delimited strings or specify more complex transforms.

prefix.description: This is the ID namespace's standard prefix. This should be from (in order of preference): [biolink-model](https://github.com/biolink/biolink-model/blob/master/project/prefixmap/biolink_model_prefix_map.json), [bioregistry](https://bioregistry.io/), or the resource that created the ID namespace. The delimiter is assumed to be ':' and should not be included.

prefix_combo.description: 2-item array: the first item is 'prefix' value for the input ID namespace, the second is 'prefix' value for the output ID namespace.

items.$comment: This is the contents of the 'prefix' sub-schema above. I can't use a $ref because json-schema does not allow $ref to refer to another $ref.

request_body.description: Specifies the request body. The annotation writer has the variables {{input_ids}} (array of IDs w/o prefix) and {{input_curies}} (array of IDs with prefix) to denote where the input IDs go in the request body. Jinja2 templating is available to transform those arrays into delimited strings or specify more complex transforms.
